aliases: Hut 8 Beacon Point AI Data Center Campus
status_detail: Hut 8 describes Beacon Point as a multi-phase AI data center campus in Nueces County with key interconnection and site approvals secured for 1,000 MW; first two phases expected to represent about $17B of capital investment. Local reporting says a second lease doubled contracted IT capacity to 704 MW and that construction/site clearing has begun, but project remains staged development rather than operational.
notes: Official developer page gives 525-acre footprint, 1,000 MW utility capacity, AI use, and $17B first-two-phase investment. County approval/incentive details appear limited because much of the site is unincorporated county land; local reports say incentives were sought but not approved.

project_name: Fort Worth Power Core / Black Mountain Parker County data-center-related development
developer: Fort Worth Power Core LLC / Black Mountain Land Company LP
status_detail: Parker County created Tax Abatement Reinvestment Zone Number 2024-03 and public notice described a tax abatement agreement for Fort Worth Power Core LP/LLC on Black Mountain Land Company property at/near 501 Pearson Ranch Road for a $500M industrial facility. Weatherford later issued a statement acknowledging public concern over data centers and related power generation projects in Parker County near Lake Weatherford, outside city limits. Local reporting says Black Mountain purchased over 2,000 acres and Fort Worth Power Core held a permit for natural gas turbines to provide backup/bridge power for a potential data center.
notes: Data-center connection is supported by city statement and local reporting, while the county tax-abatement public notice itself describes an industrial facility rather than explicitly naming a data center. Treat as early/partly opaque project lead.

project_name: TXP data center acreage in Parmer/Castro/Deaf Smith counties
aliases: Parmer County data centers discussed by Friona EDC
status_detail: Parmer County Commissioners Court minutes record Friona EDC's Wendy Carthel discussing new data centers as an option for Parmer County on April 14, 2026; April 28, 2026 minutes state Mike Brumley, TXP, had obtained about 300,000 acres in Parmer, Castro and Deaf Smith counties for data centers, described as wind and solar centers.
notes: Official minutes are sparse and do not give a specific site, facility name, MW, or approval action. Include as early county-level project lead because county minutes explicitly mention data centers and acreage across Parmer/Castro/Deaf Smith.

aliases: Amazon Pecos County data center campus
status_detail: TDLR records for Buildings A/B/C list new construction at 6000 TX-18, Fort Stockton, each 189,060 sq ft and $300M, with start date 2026-08-01 and completion date 2026-12-01. Amazon issued an official statement confirming a planned Pecos County data center campus powered by new on-site generation. News/industry reporting ties the site to GW Ranch and up to 7.65 GW of on-site natural gas generation, plus potential solar and battery storage.
notes: Capacity_mw uses reported associated on-site generation capacity (7.65 GW), not confirmed IT load. First three TDLR building filings total about 567,180 sq ft and $900M construction value.
